title: ADC quantization error budget
shortDescription: Translate a sensor error budget into the minimum ADC resolution.
statement: An ideal unipolar ADC spans 0 to 3.3 V with 2^b uniformly spaced quantization bins. A sensor produces 0.010 V per degree Celsius. Model worst-case quantization error as half a bin, using bin width 3.3 / 2^b V. What is the smallest integer b that guarantees error no greater than 0.05 degrees Celsius? Enter the bit count as a number.
constraints: Ignore noise, offset, gain error and saturation. b is a positive integer. The half-bin model is specified explicitly; do not use 2^b - 1.
objectives: Convert quantization error into physical units
Solve a logarithmic hardware sizing constraint
provenance: BitForge implementation example authored with Codex

independent.source:
from fractions import Fraction
b=1
while Fraction(33,10)/(2**b*2)/Fraction(1,100)>Fraction(1,20):
    b+=1
print(b)

explanation: The error in degrees Celsius is 3.3 / (2 × 2^b × 0.010) = 165 / 2^b. Requiring this to be at most 0.05 gives 2^b >= 3300. Thus b=12; 11 bits gives about 0.0806 degrees and 12 bits about 0.0403 degrees.
reviewNotes: Verified by an exact rational search; the statement defines the bin-width convention and excludes analog errors.
